The goal is to be a thick liquid but still watery. Rolls of spoon easily but not fast. One it boils turn down to low (simmer).

The Japanese pumpkin is normally sliced to 1/4 inch slices (like a melon) with the skin on. You can eat the skin but I don't and most other people don't either. You might be able to a half at one shot but ... Go with slices since they'll cook faster.

Simmer for 20-40 minutes until a toothpick just breaks the skin with some force.

Katsutoshi is ??? Dry Bonita flakes. It actually looks like wood shavings and taste like barbecue chips but it is actually shaved fish. You can throw some into the sauce or just put the shavings on top of the pumpkin. Heat makes them move around a bit ... Sort of ghastly when you rber they were fish before.

Strain out the pumpkin (sauce is just for flavoring while cooking) and put on nice pottery style plate with those shavings.

The cooling broth (??) should be slightly sweet but still be able to taste the other flavors.
